place: A colonnade of pale trunks on bark slabs split by seams of mist, dawn haze glowing through the gaps behind a charcoal bird with a pale halo.

source.model: authored by build agent (round 5, analyzer offline)

observations.what: Tall avian entity of calligraphic flame scrolls standing in profile-left
The bare trunk verticals: broad vertical dry sweeps dragged downward for the background trunks, the strong vertical boles on the right, and the pale halo of light between them

measured.role: Midtone atmospheric smoke and rubbed charcoal ground behind the creature
Light gray diffused background wash and middle-value forest canopy
Deep charcoal shading along the underbelly, root crevices, and shadow ribbons
Pale gray halo surrounding the crest and highlighting vertical tree barks
Maximum black linear accents defining inner volutes, eye socket boundary, and ground fissures
Transitional blending tones across the creature's breast and shaded soil
Dark gray bark textures and deep secondary folds of the plumage
Untouched paper whites forming the beak, pupil-less eye, and brightest backlights

palette.notes: Charcoal greys pushed toward violet and lavender for the haze, with lichen lime as the one warm accent on the slab tops.

motifs.name: trunk_column

motifs.name: trunk_fork
motifs.where: Leaning across a seam like the diagonal branch on the drawing's right.

shape.summary: A leaning pale trunk with a forked top, roots splayed at its base.

motifs.name: trunk_mist

shape.summary: A mist lamp: three pale lavender slabs stacked and offset on a short stone post, glowing white at the top.

motifs.name: trunk_fallen

shape.summary: A fallen pale trunk section lying on its side, dark striations along it and a lichen patch on top.

motifs.name: trunk_lintel

shape.summary: Two pale trunk posts with a leaning branch laid across as the lintel.

composition.mass: The drawing's vertical strokes stand up as a colonnade of silver trunks on four or five slabs, the seams between slabs are the gaps between trunks where mist pours through, a leaning branch makes the gate, and the pale glow behind the bird becomes a halo disc on its perch.
composition.read: Across three slabs, over the one-cell land bridges in the seams, past a fallen trunk and the mist lamps, into the colonnade where the bird stands.

lighting.notes: haze glowing behind the trunks: The analysis puts pale grey (#bcbcbc) around the crest and on the tree barks: light comes from behind the trees, so the background is bright lavender haze and the trunks read pale-edged against it.

rules: Trunks line slab edges in rows, never on the approach.
Mist lamps sit by the seam crossings.
Keep a clear ring around the bird so the halo reads.

concept.name: aspect-trunks
concept.fragment: Round 5 reading authored by the build agent from pipeline/seed/analysis/forest.json and the drawing itself, without the analyzer (Gemini returns 402). One aspect of the charcoal drawing, "trunks", becomes the place; the shaper, palette, lighting, props and the figure's pose are argued from that aspect alone. It must not repeat the round-4 forest readings (ash basin with soot trunks, taproot knoll with charred boles, birch spiral) or their shapers (basin, mound, spiral).
